summary: A first-person narrator and a companion named Tara tour a nursery room full of infants in identical wicker bassinets, while the narrator films with a Betacam in poor light. Tara, dreamy and uninterested in how the babies arrived, explains only that people bring them there and that girls take them to new mothers. Tara wants to take the babies out into the snow, and the narrator refuses, then questions a woman changing a baby, who stares in alarm and says nothing. The passage is a fragment from the middle of Book 3, part 86.
one_line: In a nursery of identical bassinets, a narrator filming with a Betacam questions Tara and a silent attendant about where the infants come from.
key_facts: Tara says the children are orphans or abandoned, from overseas or wherever, according to Ramala.
Tara says the infants are brought to the nursery by people, and the girls there take them to their new mothers.
The narrator is filming with a Betacam, though the light is not enough for broadcast quality.
The room holds at least twenty bassinets, all alike, made of wicker with a white lace hood.
The room smells like baby powder.
Tara picks up one infant and says, "Isn't this one cute? I'd so love to have him."
The baby Tara holds begins crying outright, much to her annoyance.
Tara wants to take some babies out into the snow so they can see how beautiful it is.
Ramala makes the nurses try to speak English around the children, but they don't really know much.
The narrator refuses to take the babies out into the snow tonight and suggests the morning instead.
The narrator says she does not speak the language the staff use and is not sure she could explain the idea in English.
The narrator confirms that the baby being changed is a boy.
When the narrator asks the woman changing the baby where the child came from, the woman stares in alarm and turns away.
The narrator wonders whether Paula and Carly got their babies the same way, and realizes she neglected to ask.

entities.name: Ramala
